issues.evidence: Tibetan ཚར་གཅད་བྱ་བར་ཟད (bo-kunpal 8-167: ཚར་བཅད་པར་བྱ་བར་ཟད་དོ; bo-shenga: ཚར་བཅད་པར་བྱ་བ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་དོ) means 'nothing remains but to subdue you'; the Hindi passive future drops the 'only/nothing else' force (ཟད) and the speaker's own resolve.

issues.evidence: The Tibetan གལ་ཏེ་བག་མེད་གྱུར་ནས་ཁྱོད། སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ལ་མ་བྱིན་ན has no ངས and places ཁྱོད in the clause; bo-kunpal 8-170 and bo-gyaltsab 8-170 (second gloss) read ཁྱོད (the mind) as the one who becomes heedless and does not give. The Sanskrit and bo-shenga read 'I do not give you'. The Hindi fixes one reading; a neutral rendering would keep the Tibetan's open agent.
